string.text: Polytech
A former FICT student who has kept the strength of Polyana and the prudence of Dorm 8.
Faraday
A former KPI Telecom engineer who swapped his server room for a shack at the Forestry. Plans to start a business on anonymous data storage.
Rokovoy's router
A router from the FICT lab that Rokovoy brought back from China. Whatever is in its firmware, there are plenty of people in the Zone who want to get their hands on a router like this.
Find Faraday
Polytech asked you to find Faraday, who is holding on to Rokovoy's router. He is hiding in a hut at the Forestry.
Get the router from Faraday
Faraday has the router. Talk to him and get it.
Search Faraday's body
Faraday is dead. The router should still be on his body.
Escort Faraday to the Skadovsk
Faraday will give you the router if you get him to the Skadovsk. Bandits may attack on the way.
Return the router to Polytech
You have the router. Bring it to Polytech at the Skadovsk.
Got any work for me?
There's one thing. I want to get hold of a router.
What router?

When I studied at FICT, I took the course on networks and Linux. Rokovoy taught it back then, and during labs he would sometimes take out a modified router he had brought back from his internship in China. Strange casing, and firmware nobody ever really figured out. They say the most hardcore Chinese programmers wrote it, and the Chinese firewall runs on hardware like that.
How did it end up in the Zone?

When the department was getting rid of old equipment, the exhibit went off with the rest of the decommissioned hardware to the dealers who trade in that stuff. From there it travelled down the chain into the Zone. A rumour spread fast: there's a device that can be neither hacked nor tracked. After a rumour like that, the router's quiet life was over. Suddenly everyone with something to hide wanted it. Duty and Freedom first of all: each wants its own comms to stay private, and neither wants the other to get a thing like that. As soon as the router surfaced on the local markets, a real hunt began. It changed hands several times, but nobody managed to keep it for long. So bear in mind, you won't be the first one to go after it.
And why do you need it?

Half nostalgia, half principle. It's a piece of our department and a piece of my student years. I don't want it to become a trophy in Duty and Freedom's squabbles. And honestly, I'm curious what's in that firmware myself. What if the legends are true?
And who has it now?

Last I heard, it settled with a loner called Faraday. Not much is known about him. They say he used to work at KPI Telecom, and now he's building his own closed network in the Zone, a darknet of sorts. He wants to keep the secret data of the factions and ordinary stalkers alike: a neutral, unreachable keeper of other people's secrets. Rumour has it even the FAKS archive sits on his servers. He's holed up in a hut at the Forestry. He doesn't like strangers and takes everyone for either a faction agent or a bounty hunter.
What's the FAKS archive?

Ha, that's a legend of its own. The FAKS archive is one of the greatest mysteries of KPI. Nobody really knows what's in it: the senior students of those years just smile and change the subject. But I'm sending you for the router, not the archive.
Fine, I'll find your Faraday.
Deal, then. Bring me the router and I'll pay. And I wasn't joking about Duty and Freedom: watch your back.
I've got no time for this right now.
I understand.
I've brought Rokovoy's router.

Faraday gave it up himself? They must have really pressed him if he decided to quit. Pity, the idea of a neutral vault was a beautiful one. But there's no such thing as neutral in the Zone: sooner or later they come for you anyway.
So Faraday is gone... Not for me to judge you, the Zone is the Zone. But I'm sorry for the keeper of secrets: now all of them are gone with him.
And the FAKS archive?
The FAKS archive can stay a secret. Some secrets should stay unrevealed. Hand over the router, and here's what I promised. Thank you, stalker.
Stop right there! One more step and I shoot. Who are you? What do you want?
Polytech sent me. For Rokovoy's router.

Rokovoy's? I sat his networks exam too, passed on the third try... Alright, I believe you. Listen, since you're one of ours - I've got a deal for you. Bandits have been leaning on me. They want the router: someone told them Duty and Freedom would pay good money for it. They gave me time to think, they'll be back soon. I can't hold out here alone. Get me to the Skadovsk and the router's yours.
Deal. Let's go.
Quick, then, before they're back. You go first, I'll follow.
Easier to just take the router off you right now.
Right, another one. Go on then.
They say you've got the FAKS archive.
People say all sorts of things. Even if I do, it's none of your business.
That's it, we made it.
We did. They won't get me here. Won't last, though: if not these, others will come. As long as I've got the router, that's how it'll be. Forget it. I'm shutting down.
So, about the router?
A deal's a deal. Take it, bring it to your Polytech. And... thanks.
Max
A FICE student writing a diploma on electrical anomaly patterns. Came to the Zone for fieldwork. Lost his equipment in the Iron Forest and has been stuck on the Shevchenko ever since.
FPGA development board

An FPGA development board, rescued from a pile of written-off equipment in building 18. Thousands of logic cells, a dozen fast inputs and one desperate diploma depending on it. Keep away from Electras, rain and scientific advisors.
Burnt FPGA board

Used to be an FPGA development board. Now it's a piece of black textolite that smells like a soldering lab gone wrong. Technically it still has thousands of logic cells. None of them are logical anymore.
Cheap FPGA board

A cheap FPGA board from a Chinese marketplace. Delivery took three months, the manual is in a language nobody can identify. Too weak for Polytech's scanner, but perfect for a diploma: the committee won't notice.
